questiontext.text:
The following are types of non-probabilistic sampling techniques except

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

[[ if test="member(1, ta_index)" ]]

Stratified sampling is a sampling technique used in statistics and research to ensure that the sample drawn from a population is representative and includes subgroups or strata in the same proportion as they exist in the population. It is a systematic approach to sampling that can improve the accuracy and reliability of survey results by ensuring that each subgroup within the population is adequately represented.

[[/ if ]] [[ if test="member(2, ta_index)" ]]

Systematic sampling is a probability sampling technique used in statistics and research to select a sample from a larger population in a systematic and structured way. It is an efficient method for obtaining a representative sample while maintaining simplicity in the sampling process.

[[/ if ]] [[ if test="member(3, ta_index)" ]]

Multistage sampling, also known as multi-stage cluster sampling, is a complex probability sampling technique used in statistics and research to sample from large and diverse populations. This method involves breaking down the population into multiple stages or levels, with sampling occurring at each stage. Multistage sampling is particularly useful when it is impractical or too costly to conduct a simple random sample of the entire population.

[[/ if ]]
